claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in a CrFeCoNiAl-based HEA is governed by the integrity and self-healing capacity of its passivating oxide film.
Annealing promotes formation of a robust and continuous passivating oxide layer.
The oxide film produced in the annealed state rapidly repassivates regions mechanically stripped during wear.
Rapid repassivation mitigates synergistic degradation under combined wear-corrosion conditions.
The as-cast CrFeCoNiAl-based HEA has an uneven or less uniform passivating oxide layer.
Annealing after casting can be used to promote a uniform, self-healing passivating oxide film.
Mechanical forces remove the oxide film during combined wear and corrosion.
Annealing-induced microstructural modification enhances the rate of oxide-film regeneration.
The regenerated oxide film protects the underlying alloy from degradation.
The as-cast state forms a less effective oxide film that repassivates more slowly than the film on the annealed state.
Slower repassivation in the as-cast state causes accelerated material degradation.
Under combined wear-corrosion testing, the annealed HEA will have lower material loss and less damage than the as-cast HEA.
Wear-corrosion synergy will be more pronounced in the as-cast state than in the annealed state.
Differences between annealed and as-cast samples will be less pronounced in separate wear-only and corrosion-only tests than in the combined test.
The proposed prediction applies when wear and corrosion act simultaneously under the selected load and electrolyte conditions.
Annealing-induced changes such as grain-size variation could independently dominate wear resistance and eliminate the predicted difference.
Bulk microstructural effects may contribute to differences between annealed and as-cast samples independently of surface-oxide effects.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says the annealed state's benefit should emerge most strongly under combined testing and be less stark in separate tests. The falsification rule ambiguously says that failure of separate tests to reveal synergy—parenthetically defined as the benefit emerging only under combined conditions—would falsify the hypothesis, even though that parenthetical observation matches the prediction.
The mechanism describes the as-cast film as capable of repassivation but doing so more slowly, whereas the baseline calls it non-self-healing, an absolute characterization.
